claim: Rice (Oryza sativa) genome-wide gene expression patterns in rainfed and irrigated fields during two distinct tropical seasons can be related to climatic fluctuations using simple linear models.
source: We analyzed the genome-wide gene expression patterns of rice (Oryza sativa) growing in rainfed and irrigated fields during two distinct tropical seasons and determined simple linear models that relate transcriptomic variation to climatic fluctuations.
evidence: The abstract states that the authors analyzed expression patterns and determined linear models relating them to climatic fluctuations, supported by the experimental data presented throughout the manuscript.

claim: Linear models combining multiple environmental parameters can account for patterns of expression in the field of co-expressed gene clusters.
source: These models combine multiple environmental parameters to account for patterns of expression in the field of co-expressed gene clusters.
evidence: The abstract explicitly states this finding, which is supported by the modeling results presented in the manuscript.

claim: Field type and macroclimate have broad impacts on transcriptional responses to environmental fluctuations, especially for genes involved in photosynthesis and development.
source: We found that field type and macroclimate had broad impacts on transcriptional responses to environmental fluctuations, especially for genes involved in photosynthesis and development.
evidence: The abstract states this finding, which is supported by the GO enrichment analysis and field comparison data presented in the results.

claim: Variation in solar radiation and temperature at the timescale of hours has reproducible effects across environmental contexts.
source: Nevertheless, variation in solar radiation and temperature at the timescale of hours had reproducible effects across environmental contexts.
evidence: The abstract states this finding, which is supported by the model selection results and transferability analysis with the Nagano dataset.

claim: Plants rely on transcriptional dynamics to respond to multiple climatic fluctuations and contexts in nature.
source: Plants rely on transcriptional dynamics to respond to multiple climatic fluctuations and contexts in nature.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as background knowledge about plant biology.

claim: Plants have evolved responses to complex environmental fluctuations that take place at time scales that vary from seconds to years and shape plant developmental and physiological responses.
source: Plants have evolved responses to complex environmental fluctuations that take place at time scales that vary from seconds to years and shape plant developmental and physiological responses.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the introduction.

claim: Variations in environmental signals need to be integrated and transduced to changes in gene expression, which may then be associated with physiological and/or morphological adaptations.
source: Variations in environmental signals, including temperature, water levels, solar radiation, biotic interactions and resource availability, are often unpredictable and need to be integrated and transduced to changes in gene expression, which may then be associated with physiological and/or morphological adaptations (Ahuja et al., 2010; Weston et al., 2008).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Predicting the adaptive responses occurring in natural environments is a key challenge in plant biology.
source: Predicting the adaptive responses occurring in natural environments is a key challenge in plant biology.
evidence: This is stated as a general challenge in the field, representing established knowledge.

claim: Understanding how genes and functional genetic networks are regulated in response to fluctuating stimuli in nature is necessary to predict adaptive responses in natural environments.
source: This is an undertaking that will not be achieved without understanding how genes and functional genetic networks are regulated in response to fluctuating stimuli out in nature (Richards et al., 2009).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: Studies of plant transcriptional responses to environmental perturbations are nearly exclusively undertaken in controlled, static laboratory conditions that are divergent from what is seen in the natural world.
source: Studies of plant transcriptional responses to environmental perturbations are nearly exclusively undertaken in controlled, static laboratory conditions that are divergent from what is seen in the natural world.
evidence: This is stated as an observation about the state of the field.

claim: Organismal phenotypes and the genetic architecture of various traits differ between controlled laboratory and field conditions.
source: While these laboratory experiments have enriched our knowledge of the molecular pathways involved in abiotic stimulus responses, it is clear that organismal phenotypes and the genetic architecture of various traits differ between controlled laboratory and field conditions (Malmberg et al., 2005; Mishra et al., 2012; Weinig et al., 2002).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: The improvement of crops for resistance to abiotic stresses has not met the expectations arising from advances in genomics technologies.
source: This so-called "laboratory/field (lab-field) gap" is often referred to when trying to explain why the improvement of crops for resistance to abiotic stresses, for example, has not met the expectations arising from advances in genomics technologies (Cabello et al., 2014).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: The combination of heat and drought stresses has been found to be more detrimental to crop yield than the addition of either stress alone.
source: Concurrent stresses have a major impact: the combination of heat and drought stresses, for example, has been found to be more detrimental to crop yield than the addition of either stress alone (Mittler, 2006).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: Mesophyll conductance depends on both CO2 concentration and irradiance.
source: The interplay of multiple dynamic factors also affect plants at the physiological level, particularly in the case of photosynthesis: mesophyll conductance depends on both CO2 concentration and irradiance (Kaiser, et al., 2015)
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: Drought can undermine the otherwise positive effect of high temperature on photosynthetic efficiency.
source: while drought can undermine the otherwise positive effect of high temperature on photosynthetic efficiency (Pfannschmidt and Yang, 2012).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: Some effects of combinations of multiple environmental perturbations on gene expression cannot be predicted from the individual treatments in tobacco, Arabidopsis thaliana, and sorghum.
source: Some of the effects of combinations of multiple environmental perturbations on gene expression cannot be predicted from the individual treatments, as has been shown in tobacco (Rizhsky et al., 2002a), Arabidopsis thaliana (Rasmussen et al., 2013) and sorghum (Johnson et al., 2014).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Little is known about how the levels and patterns of gene expression are modulated by multiple dynamic abiotic factors in the field.
source: Because these studies were conducted under controlled conditions, little is known about how the levels and patterns of gene expression are modulated by multiple dynamic abiotic factors in the field (Izawa, 2015).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: The extent to which the climatic or ecological context affects molecular environmental responses of interest in plants remains to be determined.
source: Thus, the extent to which the climatic or ecological context affects molecular environmental responses of interest in plants remains to be determined.
evidence: This is stated as a knowledge gap in the field.

claim: This study is the first to focus on identifying the concurrent effects of multiple environmental factors on gene expression under natural climatic fluctuations in a crop species.
source: The study we report here is the first to focus on identifying the concurrent effects of multiple environmental factors on gene expression under natural climatic fluctuations in a crop species.
evidence: The authors explicitly state this is the first study of its kind.

claim: The genetic background of the plants had limited effect on the environmental response of the global transcriptome.
source: The genetic background of the plants had limited effect on the environmental response of the global transcriptome.
evidence: This finding is stated in the introduction and supported by the genotype correlation analysis in the results.

claim: Additive effects of several environmental factors drive the field expression of multiple co-expressed gene clusters.
source: We show that additive effects of several environmental factors drive the field expression of multiple co-expressed gene clusters.
evidence: This finding is stated in the introduction and supported by the model selection results.

claim: The field context reshaped a large part of transcriptional patterns, while the effect of season was more limited.
source: We also found that the field context reshaped a large part of transcriptional patterns, while the effect of season was more limited.
evidence: This finding is stated in the introduction and supported by the field and season correlation analysis.

claim: The sensitivity to the environmental context was particularly important for groups of co-expressed genes involved in photosynthesis and development.
source: This sensitivity to the environmental context was particularly important for groups of co-expressed genes involved in photosynthesis and development.
evidence: This finding is stated in the introduction and supported by the GO enrichment analysis.

claim: Only a small part of the relationships between weather fluctuations and gene expression identified under a tropical climate could be detected in temperate conditions.
source: Finally, we used previously-published field expression data from Nagano et al. (2012) to show that only a small part of the relationships between weather fluctuations and gene expression identified under a tropical climate could be detected in temperate conditions.
evidence: This finding is stated in the introduction and supported by the transferability analysis with the Nagano dataset.

claim: The experiment was conducted during the dry season (January–February) and wet season (July–August) at the International Rice Research Institute in Los Baños, Laguna, Philippines in 2013.
source: We conducted two phases of field cultivation - one during the dry season (January–February) and one during the wet season (July–August) at the experimental rice station of the International Rice Research Institute (IRRI), Los Baños, Laguna, in the island of Luzon in the Philippines in 2013 (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is a description of the experimental design.

claim: One field was cultivated following irrigated lowland practices with shallow water under constant irrigation and transplanted seedlings.
source: One field was cultivated following irrigated lowland practices: it was flooded with shallow water under constant irrigation and seedlings were transplanted to the field after being raised for 3 weeks in seedbeds (referred to as irrigated field).
evidence: This is a description of the experimental design.

claim: The second field was managed according to upland cultivation practices: it was rainfed, not irrigated and had been directly seeded.
source: The second field was managed according to upland cultivation practices: it was rainfed, not irrigated and had been directly seeded (referred to as rainfed field).
evidence: This is a description of the experimental design.

claim: Three different landraces of rice were grown: Azucena, Pandan Wangi, and Palawan.
source: We grew three different landraces of rice: (i) Azucena, an upland adapted landrace; (ii) Pandan Wangi, traditionally used for lowland cultivation only in the dry season; and (iii) Palawan, another upland adapted landrace that is used only during wet season cultivation.
evidence: This is a description of the experimental design.

claim: Rice leaf tissue was sampled during 1 month of vegetative growth (15 sampling timepoints, 2 days apart) to avoid the major shift in gene expression patterns induced by the transition to the flowering stage.
source: To avoid the major shift in gene expression patterns induced by the transition to the flowering stage (Sato et al., 2011), which would confound our detection of environmental effects, we sampled rice leaf tissue during 1 month of vegetative growth (15 sampling timepoints, 2 days apart).
evidence: This is a description of the experimental design with a citation supporting the rationale.

claim: Sampling was carried out 4 hr after sunrise to minimize circadian-driven transcriptional variation.
source: Sampling was carried out 4 hr after sunrise to minimize circadian-driven transcriptional variation.
evidence: This is a description of the experimental design.

claim: Each sample included six young leaves, each from a different plant, to minimize variation in individual plant microenvironment.
source: Each sample included six young leaves, each from a different plant, to minimize variation in individual plant microenvironment.
evidence: This is a description of the experimental design.

claim: 22,144 genes were included in the analysis after excluding genes with low detection across samples.
source: We excluded from our analysis genes for which we detected sequencing reads for less than 20 samples out of the 60 samples in each genotype per season subset of the data. The expression data for the 22,144 remaining genes was log-transformed and the biological replicates were averaged.
evidence: This describes the data processing steps.

claim: Only 19 out of the 56 clusters (4663 genes) had a correlation coefficient between genotypes below 0.8 in the dry season.
source: Only 19 out of the 56 clusters (4663 genes) had a correlation coefficient between genotypes below 0.8 (Figure 2A).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by Figure 2A.

claim: Clusters with a low genotype correlation had a high model MSE, showing that the ED models did not adequately explain these genotype differences.
source: Clusters with a low genotype correlation had a high model MSE, which showed that the ED models did not adequately explain these genotype differences.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: 48 clusters (15,103 genes) had a correlation coefficient below 0.8 between field environments in the dry season.
source: We found much more extensive differences in gene expression patterns between field environments (Figure 2B), with 48 clusters (15,103 genes) that had a correlation coefficient below 0.8.
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by Figure 2B.

claim: All clusters with high correlation between field environments (r > 0.8) had ED models that fitted the cluster mean well (model MSE < 0.12).
source: While all clusters with high correlation between field environments (r > 0.8) had ED models that fitted the cluster mean well (model MSE < 0.12), low MSE models were also selected for several clusters with strong dissimilarities between field environments.
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by Figure 2B.

claim: ED models could explain strong field differences in some cases.
source: In some cases, ED models could thus explain strong field differences.
evidence: This is an inference from the observation that low MSE models were selected for clusters with strong field dissimilarities.

claim: The model for cluster 9 consists of a single linear equation for both fields and both seasons combining a negative term for soil moisture at 15 cm depth, a positive term for 1-hr average of solar radiation (exponentially transformed) and a positive term for the change in temperature during the last 2 hr.
source: As an example, the simple season-specific ED model selected for cluster 9 is presented in Figure 3A (Supplementary file 1A–C). The model consists of a single linear equation for both fields and both seasons. It combines a negative term for soil moisture at 15 cm depth, a positive term for 1-hr average of solar radiation (exponentially transformed) and a positive term for the change in temperature during the last 2 hr.
evidence: This describes the model for cluster 9 as shown in Figure 3.

claim: The soil moisture input parameter in the cluster 9 model allows for modeling gene expression differences between field environments while keeping a common model for both field environments.
source: In this model, the soil moisture input parameter (Figure 3B, Supplementary file 1B) allows for modeling gene expression differences between field environments while keeping a common model for both field environments, in particular the higher expression in the rainfed field environment in the dry season.
evidence: This is an interpretation of how the model works, supported by Figure 3B.

claim: The selection of a common model for the dry and wet seasons for cluster 9 shows that the gene expression response to climatic factors of this cluster was largely independent of the season.
source: The selection of a common model for the dry and wet seasons shows that the gene expression response to climatic factors of this cluster was largely independent of the season.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the model selection result for cluster 9.

claim: The median genotype correlation of all genes in the analysis was 0.55.
source: While the median genotype correlation of all genes in the analysis was 0.55, the median of all gene cluster means was 0.90, showing that averaging expression profiles over many genes remarkably reduces sources of non-replicability.
evidence: This is a statistical summary of the data.

claim: The median genotype correlation of all gene cluster means was 0.90.
source: While the median genotype correlation of all genes in the analysis was 0.55, the median of all gene cluster means was 0.90, showing that averaging expression profiles over many genes remarkably reduces sources of non-replicability.
evidence: This is a statistical summary of the data.

claim: Averaging expression profiles over many genes remarkably reduces sources of non-replicability.
source: While the median genotype correlation of all genes in the analysis was 0.55, the median of all gene cluster means was 0.90, showing that averaging expression profiles over many genes remarkably reduces sources of non-replicability.
evidence: This is an inference from the comparison of median correlations between individual genes and cluster means.

claim: 27 gene expression clusters with a genotype correlation greater than 0.9 encompass 11,371 (63%) of the 17,931 genes in the analysis.
source: We focused on 27 gene expression clusters with a genotype correlation greater than 0.9 (Figure 4, Supplementary file 1C). They encompass 11,371 (63%) of the 17,931 genes in the analysis, as they include most of the largest gene clusters.
evidence: This is a statistical summary of the data shown in Figure 4.

claim: Only 6 out of the 27 clusters (2308 genes) with high genotype correlation showed high correlation (r > 0.8) between fields in both seasons.
source: For these clusters, we observed extensive field effect on the climatic/developmental response, with only 6 out the 27 clusters (2308 genes) showing high correlation (r > 0.8) between fields in both seasons.
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by Figure 4.

claim: The dry season climatic conditions generated wider between-field differences in gene expression compared with the wet season.
source: As expected from the much lower precipitation levels during the dry season, which accentuated the difference in water availability between fields (Figure 1A), the dry season climatic conditions generated wider between-field differences in gene expression compared with the wet season (Figure 4, Supplementary file 1C).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by Figures 1A and 4.

claim: 11 out of the 27 clusters (4967 genes) with high genotype correlation were modeled with the same equation for both seasons, indicative of season-independent responses.
source: The season effect was slightly less prevalent, as 11 out the 27 clusters (4967 genes) were modeled with the same equation for both seasons (Supplementary file 1C), indicative of season-independent responses.
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by Supplementary file 1C.

claim: The six clusters in group 1 were mostly influenced by short-term climatic conditions and, to a lesser extent, developmental factors.
source: They were mostly influenced by short-term climatic conditions and, to a lesser extent, developmental factors (Figure 5B, Supplementary file 1C), suggesting that short-term temperature/solar radiation had a strong effect on gene expression variation over time that could be independent of the field environment even under limited water availability.
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by Figure 5B.

claim: Short-term temperature/solar radiation had a strong effect on gene expression variation over time that could be independent of the field environment even under limited water availability.
source: They were mostly influenced by short-term climatic conditions and, to a lesser extent, developmental factors (Figure 5B, Supplementary file 1C), suggesting that short-term temperature/solar radiation had a strong effect on gene expression variation over time that could be independent of the field environment even under limited water availability.
evidence: This is an inference from the observation that group 1 clusters showed similar patterns across fields despite differences in water availability.

claim: Cluster 9 is highly enriched for genes related to response to heat (p<10–18), response to high light intensity (p<10–9) and response to abiotic stimulus (p<10–6).
source: Cluster 9 is highly enriched for genes related to response to heat (p<10–18, hypergeometric test), response to high light intensity (p<10–9) and, more generally, response to abiotic stimulus (p<10–6), which is consistent with an induction by drought, solar radiation and/or temperature increase.
evidence: This finding is from the GO enrichment analysis.

claim: The enrichment of cluster 9 for abiotic stress response genes is consistent with an induction by drought, solar radiation and/or temperature increase.
source: Cluster 9 is highly enriched for genes related to response to heat (p<10–18, hypergeometric test), response to high light intensity (p<10–9) and, more generally, response to abiotic stimulus (p<10–6), which is consistent with an induction by drought, solar radiation and/or temperature increase.
evidence: This is an inference from the GO enrichment results and the model parameters.

claim: Four gene clusters from group 1 with models that have negative terms for short-term temperature/solar radiation are enriched for signaling/regulatory categories of genes.
source: The four gene clusters from group 1 with models that have negative terms for short-term temperature/solar radiation are enriched for signaling/regulatory categories of genes – cluster 8 for response to hormone stimulus, cluster 21 for cell communication and signaling, cluster 24 for protein kinase activity and hormone-related signaling pathway and cluster 30 for regulation of transcription, DNA-dependent.
evidence: This finding is from the GO enrichment analysis.

claim: Short-term temperature/solar radiation effects on the expression of groups of co-expressed abiotic stress response and signaling/regulatory genes can be impervious to the field environment.
source: This shows that short-term temperature/solar radiation effects on the expression of groups of co-expressed abiotic stress response and signaling/regulatory genes can be impervious to the field environment.
evidence: This is an inference from the observation that these clusters showed similar responses across field environments.

claim: The 12-gene clusters in group 2 have strong differences in gene expression pattern between the rainfed and irrigated fields that are specific to the dry season.
source: The 12-gene clusters in group 2 have in common strong differences in gene expression pattern between the rainfed and irrigated fields that are specific to the dry season.
evidence: This is a description of the characteristics of group 2 clusters based on the data.

claim: The differences in gene expression between fields for group 2 clusters are probably due in great part to the drought period experienced during the dry season.
source: These differences are probably due in great part to the drought period experienced during that season.
evidence: This is an inference from the observation that differences were specific to the dry season when drought occurred.

claim: Gene clusters in which expression was higher in the rainfed field (clusters 2, 4, 10, 12 and 31) showed an overall increase of expression over time in that field environment, consistent with an induction of expression following the decrease in soil moisture.
source: Gene clusters in which expression was higher in the rainfed field (clusters 2, 4, 10, 12 and 31) showed an overall increase of expression over time in that field environment (Supplementary file 1A), consistent with an induction of expression following the decrease in soil moisture.
evidence: This is an observation from the data with an inference about the cause.

claim: Clusters 1 and 5 are strongly enriched for genes associated with photosynthesis.
source: Among the gene clusters with a lower level of expression in the rainfed field, clusters 1 and 5 are strongly enriched for genes associated with photosynthesis.
evidence: This finding is from the GO enrichment analysis.

claim: Clusters 1 and 5 are enriched in genes related to lipid biosynthetic process and for cluster 1, secondary metabolic and carbohydrate catabolic processes.
source: Both clusters are also enriched in genes related to lipid biosynthetic process and for cluster 1, secondary metabolic and carbohydrate catabolic processes.
evidence: This finding is from the GO enrichment analysis.

claim: The enrichment of clusters 1 and 5 for photosynthesis and metabolic process genes is consistent with the deleterious effect of abiotic stress on photosynthesis and shows the consequences of that effect on the expression of genes involved in metabolic processes dependent on photosynthetic products.
source: This result is consistent with the deleterious effect of abiotic stress on photosynthesis (Chaves et al., 2009) and shows the consequences of that effect on the expression of genes involved in the metabolic processes dependent on photosynthetic products.
evidence: This is an inference from the GO enrichment results, supported by a citation.

claim: Cluster 12 had a higher level of expression in the rainfed field environment in the dry season and is modeled with positive terms for short-term temperature/solar radiation across both fields and both seasons.
source: In contrast, cluster 12 had a higher level of expression in the rainfed field environment in the dry season. Like cluster 9 in group 1, it is modeled with positive terms for short-term temperature/solar radiation across both fields and both seasons and is enriched for several categories of abiotic stimulus response genes.
evidence: This is a description of the characteristics of cluster 12 based on the data.

claim: There were two distinct main behaviors of abiotic stress response genes in the experiment: both responding to short-term temperature/solar radiation and drought but to different extents.
source: This shows that there were two distinct main behaviors of abiotic stress response genes in our experiment, both responding to short-term temperature/solar radiation and drought but to different extents.
evidence: This is an inference from comparing the behaviors of clusters 9 and 12.

claim: Clusters 4 and 31 are enriched for genes in categories related to development and phenology, like cell cycle for both, anatomical structure development and photomorphogenesis for cluster 4 and photoperiodism for cluster 31.
source: Clusters 4 and 31 also have an expression pattern consistent with induction by drought. They are both enriched for genes in categories related to development and phenology, like cell cycle for both, anatomical structure development and photomorphogenesis for cluster 4 and photoperiodism for cluster 31.
evidence: This finding is from the GO enrichment analysis.

claim: Gene clusters in groups 3 and 4 show differences between the field environments during the wet as well as the dry season, suggesting that their expression is affected by aspects of the field environment not related to water availability.
source: Gene clusters in groups 3 and 4 show differences between the field environments during the wet as well as the dry season, which suggests that their expression is affected by aspects of the field environment not related to water availability.
evidence: This is an inference from the observation that differences persisted in the wet season when water availability was similar.

claim: Cluster 6 is enriched for regulation of shoot development and developmental process.
source: Cluster 6 is enriched for regulation of shoot development and developmental process, while cluster 13 is enriched for photosynthesis genes.
evidence: This finding is from the GO enrichment analysis.

claim: Cluster 13 is enriched for photosynthesis genes.
source: Cluster 6 is enriched for regulation of shoot development and developmental process, while cluster 13 is enriched for photosynthesis genes.
evidence: This finding is from the GO enrichment analysis.

claim: Cluster 32 is enriched for genes related to thigmotropism.
source: Interestingly, this cluster is enriched for genes related to thigmotropism, the directional response to mechanical stimuli.
evidence: This finding is from the GO enrichment analysis.

claim: Out of the 45 light response genes with a strong environmental regulation, 31 were in nine clusters modeled with positive terms for short-term temperature/solar radiation while 14 were in seven clusters modeled with negative terms for short-term temperature/solar radiation.
source: Out of the 45 genes with a strong environmental regulation (Figure 6A, Supplementary file 1F), 31 were in nine clusters modeled with positive terms for short-term temperature/solar radiation while 14 were in seven clusters modeled with negative terms for short-term temperature/solar radiation.
evidence: This is a summary of the analysis of light response genes shown in Figure 6A.

claim: Most light response genes with strong environmental regulation were affected by the field environment, especially in the dry season.
source: Most of these genes were also affected by the field environment, especially in the dry season.
evidence: This is an observation from the analysis of light response genes.

claim: An ortholog of A. thaliana ELIP1 and 2 genes from cluster 15 was highly variable over time but not between fields.
source: However, one gene from cluster 15 was highly variable over time (it belonged to the 95th percentile for variance among the 17,931 genes in the 53 clusters) but not between fields. It is an ortholog of A. thaliana ELIP1 and 2 genes, which are possibly involved in pigment accumulation in response to stress (Casazza et al., 2005; Rossini et al., 2006).
evidence: This is an observation from the data with citations supporting the gene function.

claim: Transcriptional regulation is an important component of light response, especially for photoprotection and UV acclimation, and integrates responses to other abiotic stimuli linked to the field environment.
source: These results show that transcriptional regulation is an important component of light response, especially for photoprotection and UV acclimation, and integrates responses to other abiotic stimuli linked to the field environment.
evidence: This is an inference from the observation that light response genes showed responses to multiple environmental factors.

claim: Out of the 25 drought response genes with a strong environmental regulation, 10 belonged to clusters in group 2 with a low field correlation only in the dry season, indicating a drought effect on expression.
source: Out of the 25 genes from this list with a strong environmental regulation, 10 belonged to clusters in group 2 (Figure 5B) with a low field correlation only in the dry season, indicating a drought effect on expression and one gene belonged to a cluster in group 4, and showed more difference in mean expression between fields during the dry season.
evidence: This is a summary of the analysis of drought response genes.

claim: All 25 drought response genes with strong environmental regulation belonged to clusters modeled with parameters for short-term temperature/solar radiation averages or changes.
source: All 25 genes belonged to clusters modeled with parameters for short-term temperature/solar radiation averages or changes.
evidence: This is a summary of the analysis of drought response genes.

claim: For gene clusters 2, 5, 4 and 11, no temperature/solar radiation parameter was selected for the model of the rainfed field in the dry season, suggesting that these short-term climatic responses were overridden by a drought response.
source: In the case of gene clusters 2, 5, 4 and 11, however, no temperature/solar radiation parameter was selected for the model of the rainfed field in the dry season, suggesting that these short-term climatic responses were overridden by a drought response.
evidence: This is an inference from the model selection results.

claim: Genes involved in drought response may also respond to short-term temperature/solar radiation conditions.
source: Our analysis thus indicates that genes involved in drought response may also respond to short-term temperature/solar radiation conditions.
evidence: This is an inference from the observation that drought response genes were in clusters modeled with short-term climatic parameters.

claim: For drought response genes examined, a transcriptional response to variations in water availability was not always detected, but when it existed, it could be in addition to the short-term climatic response or dominate under drought conditions.
source: For the genes we examined, a transcriptional response to variations in water availability was not always detected, but when it existed, it could be in addition to the short-term climatic response or dominate under drought conditions.
evidence: This is a summary of the patterns observed for drought response genes.

claim: Twenty-eight of the 34 temperature response genes with a strong environmental regulation belonged to seven gene clusters modeled with positive terms for short-term temperature/solar radiation.
source: Twenty-eight of the 34 genes with a strong environmental regulation belonged to seven gene clusters modeled with positive terms for short-term temperature/solar radiation.
evidence: This is a summary of the analysis of temperature response genes.

claim: Several heat shock genes in clusters 9 and 12 had a greater variation over time and between fields than any selected drought-related gene.
source: Several heat shock (HS) genes in clusters 9 and 12 had a greater variation over time and between fields than any selected drought-related gene (Figures 6B and 6C, Supplementary file 1F)
evidence: This is an observation from comparing the variance of different gene groups shown in Figures 6B and 6C.

claim: The expression of several heat shock genes in cluster 18 was not affected by the field environment.
source: while the expression of several HS genes in cluster 18 was not affected by the field environment.
evidence: This is an observation from the data.

claim: In the conditions of the experiment, genes involved in temperature response were mostly induced by short-term heat or light and the results suggest frequent transcriptional integration of this response with changes in expression linked to water availability.
source: Our results show that, in the conditions of our experiment, genes involved in temperature response were mostly induced by short-term heat or light and suggest the frequent transcriptional integration of this response with changes in expression linked to water availability.
evidence: This is an inference from the analysis of temperature response genes.

claim: Non-null models were selected for 24 of the 36 PND cluster means and explained between 13 and 86% of the expression variance over the 52 data points of the PND.
source: Non-null models were selected for 24 of the 36 PND cluster means (Figure 7). They explained between 13 and 86% of the expression variance over the 52 data points of the PND.
evidence: This is a summary of the transferability analysis results shown in Figure 7.

claim: The parameters that could explain expression variation in the Philippine experiment and the PND were predominantly developmental stage and parameters for short-term solar radiation and temperature.
source: The parameters that could explain expression variation in our experiment and the PND were predominantly developmental stage and parameters for short-term solar radiation and temperature, especially in the models that explained a large part of the expression variance.
evidence: This is a summary of the transferability analysis results.

claim: Only one long-term climatic parameter was conserved in several PND cluster mean models: the 15-day average of wind speed, which was selected in four models.
source: Only one long-term climatic parameter was conserved in several PND cluster mean models: the 15-day average of wind speed, which was selected in four models, including one that explained 52% of the expression variance.
evidence: This is a summary of the transferability analysis results.

claim: A large part of climatic effects on gene expression vary with the type of climate, particularly long-term effects.
source: These results show that a large part of climatic effects on gene expression vary with the type of climate; in particular, long-term effects.
evidence: This is an inference from the transferability analysis showing limited conservation of long-term parameters.

claim: Two clusters highly enriched for genes related to photosynthesis (p<10–27 and 10–26, respectively) were both modeled with season-dependent models.
source: We identified two clusters highly enriched for genes related to photosynthesis (p<10–27 and 10–26, respectively), which were both modeled with season-dependent models.
evidence: This finding is from the GO enrichment analysis of the irrigated field data.

claim: The transcriptional response of groups of co-expressed genes involved in photosynthesis is affected by the seasonal context.
source: This result indicates that the transcriptional response of groups of co-expressed genes involved in photosynthesis is affected by the seasonal context.
evidence: This is an inference from the observation that photosynthesis-enriched clusters had season-dependent models.

claim: Cluster 13 was enriched for genes associated with the developmental process and cell cycle and was modeled with a season-dependent model.
source: Two clusters (13 and 25) were enriched for genes associated with the developmental process and cell cycle. Cluster 13 was modeled with a season-dependent model
evidence: This finding is from the GO enrichment analysis of the irrigated field data.

claim: Cluster 25 could be modeled with the same equation for both seasons of the Philippine experiment but no parameter of this equation could be transferred to model expression in the PND.
source: while cluster 25 could be modeled with the same equation for both seasons of our experiment but no parameter of this equation could be transferred to model expression in the PND.
evidence: This is a summary of the modeling and transferability results for cluster 25.

claim: The transcriptional regulation of some genes involved in development is not only sensitive to the field context but also to the season and climate type context.
source: This shows that the transcriptional regulation of some genes involved in development is not only sensitive to the field context but also to the season and climate type context.
evidence: This is an inference from the observations about clusters 13 and 25.

claim: The authors' method was more efficient in matching the Nagano et al. models with a clear environmental term than the Nagano et al. (2012) method was in the reciprocal comparison.
source: Our method was thus more efficient in matching the Nagano et al. models with a clear environmental term than the Nagano et al. (2012) method was in the reciprocal comparison.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the comparison of the two methods on the same genes.

claim: The authors' approach has a higher sensitivity to the effect of climatic factors on gene expression and the ability to detect the co-occurring effects of multiple environmental parameters.
source: This indicates that our approach has a higher sensitivity to the effect of climatic factors on gene expression, in addition to its ability to detect the co-occurring effects of multiple environmental parameters.
evidence: This is an inference from the method comparison results.

claim: The main behaviors under combined drought and short-term abiotic signals are an addition of both responses and response to either one of the stimuli, while responses specific to the combination of both stresses are rare.
source: Our results therefore show that the main behaviors under combined drought and short-term abiotic signals are an addition of both responses and response to either one of the stimuli (often integrated with a long-term climatic response), while responses specific to the combination of both stresses are rare.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the analysis of how drought affected responses to short-term climatic signals.

claim: Genes that have been previously characterized for their role in a specific type of abiotic stimulus and with a replicable expression pattern in the experiment generally displayed a transcriptional response to that stimulus.
source: Genes that have been previously characterized for their role in a specific type of abiotic stimulus – light, temperature or water availability – and with a replicable expression pattern in our experiment generally displayed a transcriptional response to that stimulus.
evidence: This is a summary of the analysis of candidate genes with known functions.

claim: In many cases, genes characterized for specific abiotic stimuli also seemed to respond to other abiotic stimuli, demonstrating the extensive connections between environmental pathways occurring in complex natural conditions.
source: In many cases, these genes also seemed to respond to other abiotic stimuli, demonstrating the extensive connections between environmental pathways occurring in complex natural conditions.
evidence: This is an inference from the observation that characterized genes showed responses to multiple environmental factors.

claim: Measuring gene expression under natural conditions and for long periods of time can help better assess the effect of multiple abiotic stimuli on gene expression.
source: Our results thus show that measuring gene expression under natural conditions and for long periods of time can help better assess the effect of multiple abiotic stimuli on gene expression.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the overall findings of the study.

claim: Most of the seasonal differences were limited to the rainfed field and were related to the prolonged period with very little precipitation occurring during the dry season.
source: Most of the seasonal differences were limited to the rainfed field and were related to the prolonged period, with very little precipitation occurring during the dry season.
evidence: This is a summary of the seasonal effects observed in the data.

claim: 44 out of 60 clusters (representing 72% of the genes in all clusters) in the irrigated field were modeled with a common equation for both seasons.
source: When analyzing only the irrigated field data, we found that 44 out 60 clusters (representing 72% of the genes in all clusters) were modeled with a common equation for both seasons (Supplementary file 1G).
evidence: This is a summary of the irrigated field analysis results.

claim: A fair level of reproducibility was observed between different years of irrigated field culture for rice.
source: A fair level of reproducibility was also observed between different years of irrigated field culture for rice (Nagano et al., 2012).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: The type of field in which rice was cultivated had a major effect on the response to climatic conditions of many genes.
source: In contrast, the type of field in which rice was cultivated had a major effect on the response to climatic conditions of many genes.
evidence: This is a summary of the field effects observed in the data.

claim: Only a small subset of the gene expression patterns observed under the tropical climate could be generalized to the temperate conditions of the Nagano et al. (2012) study.
source: We found that only a small subset of the gene expression patterns observed under the tropical climate of our experiment could be generalized to the temperate conditions of the Nagano et al. (2012) study.
evidence: This is a summary of the transferability analysis results.

claim: Results can be expected to be reproducible despite seasonal variations, but caution should be exercised about generalizing results to other climates or soil conditions.
source: This result shows that we can expect to reproduce findings about gene expression despite seasonal variations, but we should be careful about generalizing results to other climates or soil conditions than the ones their study was set in.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the reproducibility analysis across seasons and climates.

claim: Gene expression patterns driven by short-term averages of solar radiation and temperature, and to a lesser extent long-term wind speed, were the most consistent responses across seasons, fields and climates.
source: When investigating the reproducibility of transcriptional responses, we found that gene expression patterns driven by short-term averages of solar radiation and temperature, and to a lesser extent long-term wind speed, were the most consistent responses across seasons, fields and climates.
evidence: This is a summary of the reproducibility analysis.

claim: The exponentially transformed short-term averages of solar radiation (NL−) that model stronger effects of variations in the lowest range of irradiance were selected to model at least one entire season or field subset for 12 of the 27 gene clusters and could systematically be transferred from the models of the irrigated field data to explain the expression variation of the same clusters of genes observed under the Japanese temperate climate.
source: In particular, the exponentially transformed short-term averages (15 min, 1 or 4 hr) of solar radiation (NL− ) that model stronger effects of variations in the lowest range of irradiance were selected to model at least one entire season or field subset for 12 of the 27 gene clusters of our analysis and could systematically be transferred from the models of our irrigated field data to explain the expression variation of the same clusters of genes observed under the Japanese temperate climate (Supplementary file 1G).
evidence: This is a summary of the model selection and transferability results.

claim: The effect of longer-term variation (10-, 15-day averages) in temperature and solar radiation were much less reproducible across seasons, fields and climates than short-term effects.
source: In contrast, we found that the effect of longer-term variation (10-, 15-day averages) in temperature and solar radiation were much less reproducible across seasons, fields and climates than short-term effects.
evidence: This is a summary of the reproducibility analysis comparing short-term and long-term effects.

claim: Long-term environmental responses may be integrated over long periods of time, providing greater opportunity for them to be modulated by broad climatic and developmental factors.
source: One explanation is that, as these responses may be integrated over long periods of time, there is greater opportunity for them to be modulated by broad climatic and developmental factors.
evidence: This is a speculative explanation for why long-term effects are less reproducible.

claim: In nature, the effect of wind on gene expression might be more prevalent on a week-scale, which is consistent with the long-term accommodation to repetitive wind loads observed in poplar.
source: Our results show that, in nature, the effect of wind on gene expression might be more prevalent on a week-scale, which is consistent with the long-term accommodation to repetitive wind loads observed in poplar (Martin et al., 2010).
evidence: This is an inference from the observation that long-term wind speed was a reproducible parameter, supported by a citation.

claim: The GO terms for biological processes with the most significant enrichment were nucleic acid metabolic process (and its parent term nucleobase-containing compound metabolic process) and photosynthesis.
source: The GO terms for biological processes with the most significant enrichment were nucleic acid metabolic process (and its parent term nucleobase-containing compound metabolic process) and photosynthesis.
evidence: This is a summary of the GO enrichment analysis results.

claim: Nucleic acid metabolic process related genes were highly enriched in clusters 4 and 6 (p<10–18 and 10–22, respectively), which were also both enriched for developmental process and cell cycle associated genes.
source: Nucleic acid metabolic process related genes were highly enriched in clusters 4 and 6 (p<10–18 and 10–22, respectively), which were also both enriched for developmental process and cell cycle associated genes.
evidence: This is a summary of the GO enrichment analysis results.

claim: The strong enrichment in nucleic acid metabolic process related genes highlights the importance of a tight transcriptional regulation of this molecular process, probably linked to the control of cell division, in the adaptation of the developmental program to environmental fluctuations.
source: The strong enrichment in nucleic acid metabolic process related genes highlights the importance of a tight transcriptional regulation of this molecular process, probably linked to the control of cell division, in the adaptation of the developmental program to environmental fluctuations (Rymen and Sugimoto, 2012).
evidence: This is an inference from the GO enrichment results, supported by a citation.

claim: The transcriptional regulation of cell division-related aspects of growth integrates with the developmental program several time-scales of environmental stimuli.
source: As cluster 6 was modeled with several short-term environmental parameters, our results show that the transcriptional regulation of cell division-related aspects of growth integrates with the developmental program several time-scales of environmental stimuli.
evidence: This is an inference from the GO enrichment and model selection results for cluster 6.

claim: Clusters 1, 5 and 13 were greatly enriched for photosynthesis related genes (p<10–17, 10–9 and 10–19, respectively) and were all down-regulated in response to drought.
source: Clusters 1, 5 and 13 were greatly enriched for photosynthesis related genes (p<10–17, 10–9 and 10–19, respectively). These gene clusters were all down-regulated in response to drought, in accordance with previous results in A. thaliana (Chaves et al., 2009).
evidence: This is a summary of the GO enrichment analysis and expression patterns, supported by a citation.

claim: Although a large part of environmental effects on photosynthesis are regulated at the physiological and biochemical levels, the fine regulation of transcript abundance for photosynthesis genes confirms that the control of gene expression is also an important component of the modulation of photosynthetic activity.
source: Although it has been thoroughly demonstrated that a large part of environmental effects on photosynthesis are regulated at the physiological and biochemical levels (Kaiser et al., 2015), the fine regulation of transcript abundance for these photosynthesis genes shown here confirms that the control of gene expression is also an important component of the modulation of photosynthetic activity (Pfannschmidt and Yang, 2012).
evidence: This is an inference from the observed transcriptional regulation of photosynthesis genes, supported by citations.

claim: The transcriptional regulation of both photosynthesis and development relies on complex mechanisms, resulting in the integration of numerous layers of environmental cues, short-term climatic fluctuations as well as steadier aspects of the plant surroundings.
source: This suggests that the transcriptional regulation of both photosynthesis and development relies on complex mechanisms, resulting in the integration of numerous layers of environmental cues, short-term climatic fluctuations as well as steadier aspects of the plant surroundings.
evidence: This is an inference from the observations about context-dependent responses of photosynthesis and development genes.

claim: While field environments can result in complex responses, one can nevertheless identify co-expressed gene clusters the mean expression of which can be accurately modeled with climatic, field, seasonal and developmental factors.
source: Our results suggest that while field environments can result in complex responses, one can nevertheless identify co-expressed gene clusters the mean expression of which can be accurately modeled with climatic, field, seasonal and developmental factors.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the overall findings of the study.

claim: The mean daytime temperature was 26.8°C for the dry season and 27.6°C for the wet season.
source: During our experiment, the mean daytime temperature was 26.8°C for the dry season and 27.6°C for the wet season.
evidence: This is a measurement from the experimental conditions.

claim: The total precipitation during the experiment period was 84.5 mm in the dry season and 427 mm in the wet season.
source: The total precipitation during the experiment period was 84.5 mm in the dry season and 427 mm in the wet season.
evidence: This is a measurement from the experimental conditions.

claim: Precipitation of more than 1 mm was observed for 6 out of the 29 days of the dry season experiment and 22 out of the 29 days of the wet season experiment.
source: Precipitation of more than 1 mm was observed for 6 out of the 29 days of the dry season experiment and 22 out of the 29 days of the wet season experiment (Supplementary file 2).
evidence: This is a measurement from the experimental conditions.

claim: Each sample provided a mean of 58 million sequencing reads.
source: Each sample provided a mean of 58 million sequencing reads.
evidence: This is a description of the sequencing data.
